The aliases are the service's name, its domain, its operator's name in the forms the field uses ('Spawning AI', 'Spawning's') and the registry the cards and the own page name (the census keeps the registry apart, negative_tags[4], and the alias finds candidates only). Spawning as a bare word is not an alias (it is a common verb in the archive: 'sub-agent spawning'). Kudurru, Source.Plus, LAION, Stability AI and Hugging Face are distinct entities. The census's tll_reading applies #186 and #1543 (the training side of the layer; the receiving party) to the entity: that reading is the archive's, ledgered as TLL-NN. #186 and #1543, the census's anchors, are read at the passages on training corpora, inclusion in them, the measurement of machine reception and the institutional training loop. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the entity and says something of it; R where it states a relation between the entity and an archive object; O-class where a sentence applies an archive category (adversarial resistance, the defensive posture, declared inclusion in training corpora, measured reception) to one of the three classes; a checklist line, a robots.txt listing or a deployment note without a claim is not a claim.
